evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.199: apud jūdicēs causam agere (Lewis & Short, s.v. jūdex)
terms.comment: In the Roman criminal courts the case was decided by a body of jūdicēs under a presiding magistrate: they are the jury, and one of them is a juror, jūdex (see judge). Cicero’s speeches address them as jūdicēs.

terms.gloss: the jury as a body, a bench
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 8: ex senātū in hoc cōnsilium dēlēctī estis propter sevēritātem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A council; of a court, the panel of jurors who give the verdict. Its everyday senses are advice, a plan and judgement.

phrases.latin: ex senātū in hoc cōnsilium dēlēctī estis propter sevēritātem
phrases.english: you were chosen from the senate for this jury because of your strictness

sources: Lewis & Short: judex · Lewis & Short: consilium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 195, checked against the searchable text of the book.
